circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: Located on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi, the Yas Marina Circuit is a 5. 281 km track designed by Hermann Tilke that has served as the Formula One season finale since 2009. The venue represents the second of four Middle Eastern Formula One venues to be constructed, following Bahrain and preceding circuits in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: A street circuit encircling Albert Park Lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb, this track hosts the annual Formula One Australian Grand Prix along with supporting motorsport events and holds FIA Grade 1 certification. The venue has become a staple of the international racing calendar and serves multiple racing series throughout the year.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, this 4. 326-kilometer circuit originally operated as the Österreichring and was the venue for the Austrian Grand Prix across 18 consecutive seasons during the 1970s and 1980s. Following a reconstruction and shortening of the track, it was renamed and returned to hosting the Austrian Grand Prix from 1997 to 2003.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street course in Azerbaijan's capital city, situated along Baku Boulevard, with a lap distance of 6. 003 kilometers that ranks as the fourth-longest Formula One circuit. The venue first hosted the 2016 European Grand Prix before becoming the permanent home of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from 2017 onwards.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit is a 5. 412 km motorsport facility that hosted the Middle East's inaugural Formula One Grand Prix and continues to stage the annual race alongside various other motorsport events. The track, which holds a Grade 1 FIA license and features multiple configurations, has accommodated diverse racing series including endurance competitions and previously welcomed touring car championships.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, this 4. 657-kilometer Spanish circuit features a balanced mix of extended straights and diverse corner configurations, making it a comprehensive test for racing machinery. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 status and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstand facilities.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: Situated in the Walloon region of Belgium near the town of Spa, this 7. 004 km circuit has been a staple of Formula One racing since the sport's inaugural 1950 season. The venue has hosted the Belgian Grand Prix annually since 1985, with only two exceptions in 2003 and 2006, establishing itself as one of the championship's most enduring and prestigious racing destinations.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve is a 4. 361 km temporary street circuit that hosts the Formula One Canadian Grand Prix. Beyond Formula One, the venue has accommodated various international racing series including sports car championships and North American open-wheel competitions.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: Located in Shanghai's Jiading District, this Chinese motorsport facility has primarily served as the home of the Chinese Grand Prix, which ran annually from 2004 to 2019 before returning in 2024. The venue expanded its racing calendar in 2024 to include the Shanghai ePrix alongside the traditional grand prix event.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Located near villages in Northamptonshire, Silverstone has been England's premier racing venue since hosting the inaugural British Grand Prix in 1948 and the first-ever World Championship race two years later. Following decades of rotating the prestigious event between multiple circuits, the British Grand Prix became the track's permanent fixture from 1987 onwards, though Silverstone continues to welcome other major motorsport competitions including motorcycle racing.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring, located near Budapest in Hungary, is a 4. 381 km circuit that hosted the first Formula One Grand Prix held in a Soviet-bloc country when it debuted in 1986. Built in just eight months starting from October 1985, the track was constructed outside the city near a major highway after government officials rejected plans for a street circuit in Budapest's central park.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Located near Monza in northern Italy, the Autodromo Nazionale is a 5. 793 km circuit constructed in 1922 as the third purpose-built racing venue globally and Europe's oldest on the mainland. The Italian Grand Prix has been staged there continuously since 1949, except for a 1980 closure during renovation, earning the track its "Temple of Speed" nickname through its characteristic long straights and fast-flowing corners.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit is a 5. 807-kilometre Japanese motorsport venue in Mie Prefecture, operated by Honda Mobilityland. With a capacity of 155,000 spectators, it has become the primary host for Formula One racing in Japan and a cornerstone of the Super Formula championship.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course that winds through Paradise, Nevada, incorporating the famous Las Vegas Boulevard and its surrounding entertainment district. The track features passage past several iconic venues including MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: The Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez is a 4. 304 km circuit in Mexico City named after two Mexican racing drivers, Ricardo and Pedro Rodríguez, who both died in racing accidents during the 1960s and 1970s. The venue has hosted the Mexican Grand Prix during two earlier periods on a different configuration, most recently in 1992, before resuming as a regular Formula One fixture from 2015 onwards under the current Mexico City Grand Prix designation.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, Florida, spanning 3. 363 miles with 19 corners and qualifying speeds averaging 139 mph. Designed specifically for Formula One racing by specialist circuit designers, the venue joined the F1 calendar in 2022 as the home of the Miami Grand Prix.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Monaco Grand Prix takes place on a 3. 337 km street circuit that winds through the Monte Carlo and La Condamine districts, circling the harbour of this tiny principality. Despite traversing multiple neighbourhoods, the track is officially known as Monte Carlo due to its predominant location within that area.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch coastal dunes near Amsterdam, Zandvoort's 4. 259-kilometer track hosted the Dutch Grand Prix after rejoining Formula One in 2021 following a lengthy absence from the calendar. The venue's association with the sport concludes in 2026.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit, situated north of Doha in Qatar, is a 5. 419-kilometer track featuring a 1. 068-kilometer main straight and holding FIA Grade 1 certification.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos is a 4. 309 km counterclockwise racing circuit in São Paulo, Brazil, originally opened in 1940 and later renamed in 1985 to commemorate Formula One driver José Carlos Pace, who perished in an aviation accident eight years earlier. The venue hosts major motorsport events and features an adjacent kart track dedicated to fellow Brazilian racing legend Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street track situated along Saudi Arabia's Red Sea waterfront that has served as the venue for the Formula One Saudi Arabian Grand Prix since its debut in 2021 and also welcomes Formula E racing from 2025 onward.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through downtown Singapore's waterfront district, incorporating the Downtown Core and Kallang planning areas into its racing layout.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, Spain, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya spans 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced mix of lengthy straightaways and diverse corner configurations that test multiple driving skills. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification and accommodates over 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: Located in Austin, Texas, the Circuit of the Americas is a 3. 426-mile FIA Grade 1 facility that serves as the permanent home of the Formula One United States Grand Prix. The venue hosts multiple racing series including MotoGP's Americas round and the Lone Star Le Mans endurance championship, alongside its previous tenure with various other international motorsport competitions.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a Thai and British motorsport competitor who represents Thailand in Formula One while driving for Williams.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso competes for Aston Martin in Formula One, where he has claimed two World Championships during his 23-season career with 32 race victories. Beyond single-seaters, Alonso has achieved remarkable success in endurance motorsport, including two Le Mans wins and a 2018-19 World Endurance Championship, making him the sole driver to accomplish both an F1 and World Sportscar/World Endurance Championship.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Andrea Kimi Antonelli, an Italian driver, joined Mercedes in Formula One starting from 2025 and has already secured six race victories in his early career.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Haas, competing at the highest level of motorsport.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian driver Gabi Bortoleto currently races in Formula One for Audi, competing at the sport's highest level.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Valtteri Bottas, a Finnish driver currently racing for Cadillac in Formula One, achieved two runner-up finishes in the drivers' championship during his tenure with Mercedes in 2019 and 2020. Across his 13-season career, he has accumulated 10 Grand Prix victories.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Alejandro Colapinto represents Argentina in Formula One, currently racing for Alpine as a contemporary competitor in the sport.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Jack Doohan is an Australian driver who races in European endurance competition for Nielsen Racing while holding a reserve driver position with Haas in Formula One. He made appearances in seven Grand Prix events during the 2024-2025 season.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One driver currently competing for Alpine. The driver achieved a notable victory at the 2020 Italian Grand Prix while racing for AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Hadjar is a French-Algerian driver who currently races for Red Bull Racing in Formula One, competing under the French national flag.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver currently competing for Ferrari, holding a joint-record seven world championship titles alongside Michael Schumacher. He stands atop the sport's all-time records for race victories, pole positions, and podium appearances.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races for Audi in Formula One, bringing extensive experience from his long career in the sport. Beyond his F1 commitments, he has achieved significant success in endurance racing, notably capturing the prestigious 24 Hours of Le Mans title in 2015 while driving for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson, a New Zealand racing driver, currently races in Formula One for the Racing Bulls team.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Charles Leclerc is a Monaco-based racing driver currently competing for Ferrari in Formula One. He finished second in the 2022 championship standings and has secured nine Grand Prix victories throughout his nine seasons in the sport.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen, a Danish driver known as K-Mag, raced in Formula One across two separate periods spanning 2014-2020 and 2022-2024. He currently competes in the World Endurance Championship for BMW with WRT and combines this with part-time NASCAR commitments driving for Trackhouse Racing.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris, a British driver, secured the 2025 Formula One World Drivers' Championship while racing for McLaren. Throughout his eight seasons in the sport, he has accumulated 12 Grand Prix victories.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Haas. The veteran competitor achieved his sole Grand Prix victory in 2021 at the Hungarian Grand Prix while driving for Alpine.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Sergio "Checo" Pérez represents Mexico in Formula One, currently driving for Cadillac. The accomplished competitor finished second in the 2023 drivers' championship while with Red Bull and has secured six Grand Prix victories throughout his 15-year career in the sport.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Australian driver Oscar Piastri represents McLaren in Formula One, where he has secured nine race victories during his four-year stint in the championship.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Daniel Ricciardo, an Australian driver known by the nickname "the Honey Badger", competed in Formula One throughout a 14-season span ending in 2024, during which he claimed victories in eight Grand Prix races.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: George Russell represents Mercedes in Formula One competition as a British driver, having claimed seven race victories throughout his eight campaigns in the sport.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz competes for Williams in Formula One, where he has secured four Grand Prix victories throughout his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American driver currently racing in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category with Proton Competition. The former Formula One competitor, who drove in the series during 2023 and 2024, previously contested IMSA's LMP2 class with Era Motorsport.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian racing driver currently competing in Formula One for the Aston Martin team.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda, a Japanese motorsport competitor, has held reserve driver positions with Red Bull Racing and its sister team Racing Bulls during his Formula One tenure spanning 2021 to 2025.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: The Dutch driver competes for Red Bull Racing and has secured four consecutive world championship titles between 2021 and 2024. Across his 12-season Formula One career, he has accumulated 71 Grand Prix victories.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu, China's sole Formula One competitor, raced in the championship from 2022 through 2024 before transitioning to a reserve role with Cadillac. He continues to represent his nation in the sport, holding the distinction of being the only Chinese driver to have competed in Formula One.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: Operating from its Enstone base since 2021 as Alpine, this French-licensed team represents Renault's works effort in Formula One until the manufacturer's withdrawal at season-end 2025. The squad claimed a single victory under the Alpine banner through Esteban Ocon's 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix triumph and currently competes with Mercedes powerplants, having previously used the same supplier during its Lotus incarnation in 2015.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: The current iteration of Aston Martin's Formula One operation competes under the AMR GP Limited entity as Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team, continuing a British marque's long history of participation in the sport.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, the racing arm of the Italian luxury automaker, is Formula One's longest-running and most accomplished team, participating in every world championship since the sport's inception in 1950. Known colloquially as "the Prancing Horse" after their iconic emblem, Ferrari has established itself as a defining force throughout the championship's history.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: An American-licensed Formula One team founded by NASCAR owner Gene Haas, the squad entered the championship in 2016 and has been led by team principal Ayao Komatsu since January 2024, following Guenther Steiner's departure after eight years in the role.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: Founded by Peter Sauber in 1970, this Swiss engineering company established itself through endurance racing success, including overall victory at Le Mans in 1989, before entering Formula One in 1993 as an independent constructor. Following decades of competition with various transformations, the team competed through 2024 as one of the sport's longest-serving outfits before its acquisition by Audi to become the foundation for Audi's factory F1 programme.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing Limited is a British Formula One outfit headquartered at its technological facility in Woking, with operations controlled by the McLaren Group and ultimately owned by Mumtalakat Holding Company.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has maintained a presence in Formula One since 1954, both as a constructor and engine supplier. The current Mercedes-AMG Petronas outfit, based in Brackley, operates under a German licence and became a three-way partnership in 2022 when Ineos joined Mercedes-Benz Group and Toto Wolff as equal stakeholders. The team is traditionally known as the "Silver Arrows.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team established in 2024, operating as a constructor alongside its sister team Red Bull Racing under Austrian ownership. Based in Faenza with a secondary facility in Milton Keynes, the team represents Red Bull's second factory outfit in the sport's grid.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that entered the sport in 2024, operating as a second team under Red Bull GmbH's ownership. Based in Faenza with operations near its sister team in Milton Keynes, the squad competes alongside Red Bull Racing as part of the Austrian conglomerate's dual-team structure.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Red Bull Racing is an Austrian-licensed Formula One team founded in 2005 and headquartered in England, currently operating as Oracle Red Bull Racing. Under long-time team principal Christian Horner until early 2025, it became one of two Red Bull GmbH-owned racing operations alongside Racing Bulls. The team was succeeded by Laurent Mekies as team principal following Horner's departure.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering is a British Formula One constructor founded in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, succeeding Williams's earlier failed racing venture. Based in Grove, Oxfordshire, the team competes in the 2026 season as Atlassian Williams F1 Team and operates from a substantial purpose-built facility.
